entry_state: Award accounting distinguishes service and non-market conditions from market conditions, cash remeasurement from grant-date equity measurement, and the employee's settlement choice from the entity's. Beneficial amendments preserve original cost and add modification-date value over its own service period; cash-to-equity changes reconcile the existing liability rather than always adding a positive expense.
exit_state: Participation rights allocate earnings between classes before division; dividends are allocations rather than another expense. Assumed option proceeds include future services, and assumed share settlement may change earnings as well as shares. A senior cumulative entitlement and participation cap now replace the simple proportional allocation.
findings: Profit120 allocates100 to ordinary and20 to participating shares under the supplied rights, giving EPS1 and2, not ordinary EPS1.2.
Future service value changes option incremental shares from five to three; the separate settlement-choice example must reverse the absent liability expense in its assumed equity world.

sections/awards-participation.tex:subsec.entry_belief: Award recognition does not determine the earnings rights of each share class.
sections/awards-participation.tex:subsec.open_question: Which earnings belong in each class's per-share numerator?
sections/awards-participation.tex:subsec.parent_contribution: Connects ownership rights to EPS attribution before dilution.
sections/awards-participation.tex:subsec.belief_update: Dividends and residual participation determine class allocations; assumed settlement also changes its relevant earnings effects.
sections/awards-participation.tex:subsec.exit_question: How do a senior dividend and a cap change that allocation?
sections/awards-participation.tex:subsec.removal_verdict: Without this section total profit could be assigned entirely to ordinary shares.
sections/awards-participation.tex:subsec.swap_verdict: It follows award recognition so expense and per-share reporting remain distinct.
sections/awards-participation.tex:subsec.entry_verdict: The opening states the actual dividend and residual rights before the numerical weights.
sections/awards-participation.tex:subsec.exit_verdict: The final choice example retains continuing control, ordering and time weights.
sections/awards-participation.tex:subsec.promise_verdict: The120profit example and the service-proceeds example answer different explicit attribution questions.
sections/awards-participation.tex:subsec.distinct_contribution_verdict: It separates award expense, dividend allocation and hypothetical dilution rather than treating them as one computation.
